_comment: Shahnama of Firdausi, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. II: Piran saves Farangis; birth and boyhood of Kai Khusrau. Paraphrase passages with notes.

title.en: Piran Rescues Farangis and the Dream of a Newborn King
title.zh: 皮蘭救法蘭吉斯與新生王之夢

region.zh: 阿弗拉西亞卜王庭（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. II, Siyawush secs. 57-58

summary.en: Afrasiyab would slay his own pregnant daughter Farangis with her husband; Piran, riding day and night with ten remounts, reaches the court as the deathsmen stand about the portal: thou hast slain Siyawush though innocent, and now hast ill-treated thine own child; if the king would make my spirits bright, let him send Farangis to mine abode. The king grants it, and Piran bears her unhurt to Khutan. One dark and moonless night Piran dreams a splendour that outshone the sun itself, with Siyawush enthroned and sword in hand: rest no more, for from to-day new feasts and customs date, because to-night is born Shah Kai Khusrau.
summary.zh: 阿弗拉西亞卜欲殺懷孕的親生女兒法蘭吉斯；皮蘭日夜兼程、換馬十匹趕到——刑吏已列於殿門：「你弑無辜的西亞瓦什，如今又要害己女；若王要寬我心，就把法蘭吉斯交給我吧。」王允之，皮蘭安然將她送往忽檀。一個無月的黑夜，皮蘭夢見勝過太陽的榮光——西亞瓦什按劍高坐：「勿再貪睡！今夜誕生了卡伊霍斯勞王！」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: Piran on hearing this cried out in wrath, descended to the street and from the stable brought forth ten roadsters up to warriors' weight, and with the brave Ruh and Farshidward sent up the dust forthwith. He reached the court in two days and two nights, there found the deathsmen about the portal, Farangis bereft of all her wits dragged roughly by the guard with sword in hand, and all the court in uproar. The populace, men, women, and young children, were talking at the palace-gate and saying: it were a cruel, fearful, shocking deed to cut asunder Farangis! This fury will wreck the reign and none will call him king henceforward.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush sec. 57 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: When noble Farangis saw him her cheeks were hidden by a flood of tears, and she said: ill hast thou dealt with me! Why hast thou flung me while living into fire? Piran dropped off his steed, rent the raiment that he wore as paladin, and sought Afrasiyab in haste: thou hast slain Siyawush though innocent, and flung his name and kingship to the dust; thou wilt repent of this for many a day. If now the king would make my spirits bright, let him send Farangis to mine abode; have patience only till the child is born.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush sec. 57 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: He answered: do as thou hast said, for thou hast made me cease to wish to shed her blood. Piran rejoiced, sought the court-gate, rescued Farangis, bestowing many a curse upon the guards, then bore her to the country of Khutan unhurt, amid the applause of camp and court. Time passed by, and the Moon grew near to her delivery.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush sec. 57 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: One dark and moonless night, while birds, wild beasts, and cattle slept, Piran in dream beheld a splendour that outshone the sun itself, while Siyawush, enthroned and sword in hand, called loudly to him, saying: rest no more! Throw off sweet sleep and think of times to come, for from to-day new feasts and customs date, because to-night is born Shah Kai Khusrau! The chieftain roused him from his sweet repose: Gulshahr the sunny-featured woke, and came hasting to the Moon and saw the prince already born; she went with cries of joy that made the palace ring again back to Piran the chief.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush sec. 58 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

region.zh: 卡魯爾山牧場（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. II, Siyawush secs. 59-60

summary.en: Afrasiyab, warned by an adviser that a king of noble birth will lift his head from the seed of Tur and Kai Kubad, has the infant sent to the shepherds of Mount Kalur. At seven his prowess tells the secret of his birth; at ten he fights boars, wolves, lions, and leopards with a rude wooden bow. Afrasiyab swears a royal oath of safety before Piran presents the boy, charging him to appear as an alien and speak insanely; before the king the child answers about leopards only, and love at length prevails within the tyrant's heart.
summary.zh: 謀士告誡：圖爾與卡尤巴德血脈中將出現君王。阿弗拉西亞卜便將嬰兒送往卡魯爾山牧羊人處。七歲時勇武已洩露身世；十歲時憑一支粗木弓獵殺野豬、狼、獅、豹。皮蘭先讓暴君立下安全誓言，再囑少年裝傻充愣、答非所問；王座之前，孩子只談獵豹——最後連暴君心中愛意也佔了上風。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: Piran had shepherds called from Mount Kalur, to whom he spake about the infant prince, then trusted to their care his Heart and Eyes, and said: entreat him like your souls; no wind or dust must see him. They said: we will obey. He furnished them, and sent a nurse to tend the royal babe; they took the young prince with them to the mountains. Now when the brave young prince was seven years old his prowess told the secret of his birth; at ten he was a valiant warrior, who fought with boars and wolves, anon with lions and leopards, armed with that rude weapon only.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush sec. 59 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Afrasiyab spake about the past: my heart is vexed by thoughts and grief too hard to put aside; this child of Siyawush hath, so to speak, o'ercast my day; but will high policy allow a shepherd-swain to rear one of the race of Faridun? But while the child suspecteth not the past let him be glad; still, if he showeth any evil bent, he, as his father did, must lose his head.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush sec. 60 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Piran replied: this boy is as mad folk are; a child brought up by shepherds on the mountains is like wild animals; what can he know? If at this time the king shall order me, I will present this lauded youth to him, but make me easy by a promise first and swear by such an oath as kings employ. The wits of fierce Afrasiyab were lulled at hearing this, he swore a royal oath by white day and by sombre night, by God the Omnipotent: no harm shall come upon the boy through me.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush sec. 60 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Piran equipped him with a royal crown and belt and called for him a pretty palfrey whereon the shrewd, young hero sat and rode toward the palace of Afrasiyab. When he arrived Piran the general took him before the king. The king remembering his pledge and spurning all fell designs gazed in astonishment upon that royal neck. O youthful shepherd, said Afrasiyab, describe to me thy life by day and night. Khusrau thus answered him: there is no game; besides I have not arrow, bow, or string. Where'er there is a leopard the hearts of valiant warriors are rent. There was a pause; the monarch's face relaxed, and love at length prevailed within his heart.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush sec. 60 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
